rows.description: A teenager whose friend failed an exam says it was obvious, ignoring that the outcome looked open beforehand. Judging past choices by known results is unfair to the decider.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A team reviewing a failed event says the risk was obvious. A fair reviewer asks what was actually known when the choice was made, not what is known now.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A mature lead writes down forecasts and reasons before outcomes, so later reviews compare the decision process with luck and information, and fewer people are wrongly blamed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child keeps eating food he dislikes because it was paid for or keeps playing a boring game because he has already spent an hour. Past effort feels like a reason to continue.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Stuck in coaching or a course [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager continues a subject or a coaching class he hates because of the fees and years already invested. Fear of wasting the past costs him his future time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student stays in a degree or relationship that no longer fits because leaving would make earlier years feel wasted. The past cannot be recovered but the future can still be chosen.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young worker feels forced to continue an expensive plan because parents already spent money or pride on it. Others' sunk costs become moral pressure that needs a kind, honest conversation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A wise person asks if she would start this today knowing what she knows now. If not, she grieves the cost, learns from it, and moves on without shame.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child cries harder over losing a marble than he celebrates winning one. Giving up something owned feels heavier than getting an equal thing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Fear of losing rank or friends [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager avoids trying a new sport or friend group because losing his current standing feels worse than any possible gain. Safe choices shrink his world.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
